errors.oidcGeneric: Sign-in failed (code: {code}). Try again, or use a local account.
errors.oidcNotAuthorized: This account is not allowed to sign in. Ask an administrator to add your e-mail or OIDC identifier to the access list.
errors.oidcInvalidState: The SSO request was rejected (invalid, expired or replayed state token). Try again.
errors.oidcIdpError: The identity provider rejected the sign-in request. Contact the IdP administrator.
errors.oidcIdpUnreachable: The identity provider is unreachable. Try again later, or sign in with a local account below.
errors.oidcInternal: An unexpected error occurred during SSO sign-in. Try again, or use a local account.

server.user_username_invalid: The username must be 3 to 32 characters, using a–z, 0–9, _ or -.
server.user_display_name_too_long: The display name is too long.
server.user_role_invalid: Choose a role: viewer or admin.
server.user_password_too_short: The password is too short — 15 characters minimum.
server.user_email_on_oidc_allowlist: {email} is already an SSO identity. Creating a local account for it would give that person two accounts — one password-based, one federated — and which one they land in would depend on which button they pressed.
server.redirect_target_scheme: {target} must start with http:// or https://.
server.redirect_target_has_path: {target} already carries a path ({path}). With “keep the visitor's path” on, their path is appended, which would produce {host}{path}/… — either drop the path from the target, or turn that option off.
server.route_maintenance_and_redirect: A route cannot be in maintenance and redirecting at the same time.
server.redirect_self_loop: The target points back at {host}, which this route answers for: every visitor would be redirected to the same place forever. Redirect to a different host, or use a path rule to send one path elsewhere.
server.path_rule_uppercase: The path {path} contains an uppercase letter. Path matching is case-insensitive, so a prefix is stored lowercase to read the way it behaves — use {lower}.
server.path_rule_empty: The rule on {path} must declare at least one of: basic auth, an identity provider, an IP filter, a rate limit, an upstream, or a redirect.
server.path_rule_redirect_target_required: The redirect on {path} needs a target.
server.path_rule_redirect_status: The redirect status on {path} must be 301 or 302 (got {status}).
server.path_rule_redirect_target_invalid: The redirect target on {path} must be a path starting with / or a full http(s) URL (got {target}).
server.path_rule_redirect_loop: The target {target} is matched by the rule on {path} itself, so every visitor would be redirected to it forever. Point it outside the rule's own path.
server.listen_needs_capability: Cannot listen on {addr}: ports below 1024 need a capability. Add AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to the arenet systemd unit — or publish the port in docker-compose.yml when running in a container — then restart Arenet.
server.listen_port_taken: Cannot listen on {addr}: something else on this host already holds it.

errors.passphrase_required: This backup is encrypted: enter its passphrase.
errors.passphrase_invalid: Wrong passphrase (or the file was altered).
errors.passphrase_too_short: The passphrase must be at least {min} characters.
errors.backup_dir_unwritable: Arenet cannot write in {dir}: check the mount and the permissions (UID 65532 in Docker). Details: {detail}
errors.route_check_rolled_back: Change undone: {host} answered before this change and stopped answering after it ({detail}). The previous version is back in place — fix the change (upstream address, port…) and save again.
errors.route_check_rolled_back_health_check: Change undone: {host} answered before this change and stopped answering after it ({detail}). The cause is this route's own active health check, which has just marked its backends down — the upstream address and port are fine. Check the health check's URI, expected status and expected body: a probe that does not match what the backend actually answers takes the route out of service.
errors.route_check_rolled_back_maybe_health_che: Change undone: {host} answered before this change and stopped answering after it ({detail}). No upstream was available. Two places to look: the backend itself, and this route's active health check — a probe whose URI, expected status or expected body does not match what the backend answers takes the route out of service even though the backend is up.

accessLog.title: HTTP access log
accessLog.subtitle: Writes every request to a file so CrowdSec can detect what is attacking this host. Off, CrowdSec still enforces the community blocklist but detects nothing local.
accessLog.enableHint: Records every visitor's IP address and the URLs they request. That is what a detection engine needs, and it is also personal data on your disk — which is why this is off until you turn it on.
accessLog.resolvedHint: Point your CrowdSec acquisition at this path, with type: caddy, and install the crowdsecurity/caddy collection.
accessLog.pathHint: Leave empty for the default shown above. Must be absolute. Under systemd the default is /var/log/arenet; in a container it stays inside the data volume, where it survives the container being replaced.
accessLog.redactHint: The value of these parameters is replaced with REDACTED in the logged URI. Matched case-insensitively, separated by commas. The request sent to the backend is not changed. Empty means nothing is masked.
accessLog.ceiling: At most about {mb} MB on disk before compression.

check.failed: {host} is saved but does not answer: {detail}. Check that its backend is running.
check.pendingCertificate: {host} is saved; its TLS certificate is still being issued — try the route again in a minute.

list.filterPlaceholder: Filter by host, alias, upstream, redirect target…
list.statusNotMonitoredTooltip: No active health check on this route, so no upstream state is observed.
list.statusUnknownTooltip: Health check enabled, no signal received yet (warm-up window). The badge updates on the next probes.
list.statusNotApplicableTooltip: This route proxies nothing, so it has no upstream state: it answers the redirect itself.
list.postureInertTooltip: This route proxies nothing, so none of the per-route gates are applied to its traffic.

panel.emptyHint: Select a route on the left to edit it, or click
panel.pivotsAfterSave: Metrics and security open after the first save
panel.stripThinData: too few requests for a p95
panel.stripPartialHint: Request counts cover the full window. The percentiles and the bytes figure do not: part of this window was recorded before Arenet stored latency distributions, and those hours cannot be recomputed. All three line up again once the whole window is newer than the upgrade.
panel.stripNoHistogram: latency not recorded for this window
panel.stripNoHistogramHint: This window predates Arenet storing latency distributions. The requests were counted, but the distribution needed for a percentile was not kept and cannot be recomputed. Figures appear as new hours are recorded.

delete.title: Delete route
delete.confirmText: Are you sure you want to delete the route for
delete.warning: Caddy will be reloaded immediately. This action cannot be undone.

discardDialog.title: Discard your changes?
discardDialog.message: This route has unsaved changes. Leaving now drops them.

wafCRSDialog.title: Disable the OWASP CRS rules?
wafCRSDialog.message: You are about to stop loading the OWASP Core Rule Set on this route. Protection against SQLi, XSS, RCE, LFI and Protocol attacks will no longer be active. Use this only for trusted internal APIs (LAN) or legacy routes generating recurring false-positives. You can undo this action at any time by ticking the checkbox back.

toasts.connectionLost: The connection was cut while Caddy reloaded (this happens over HTTP/3). The server still applied the change and its check — the list below shows the real state. If your change is missing, the check undid it (see the audit log).

form.upstreamTlsServerNameHelper: Presented in SNI and verified against the backend’s certificate. Leave empty to use the upstream address.
form.tlsEnableHelper: Public domain required for Let's Encrypt; localhost / .local will fall back to internal CA.
form.tlsUseDedicatedCertLabel: Use a dedicated cert for this route (opt out of the wildcard)
form.tlsUseDedicatedCertHelper: Use this for routes that need a separate key (e.g. payments, staging) — the route will request its own ACME cert alongside the wildcard.
form.healthCheckExpectStatusHint: 0 accepts any 2xx. 1 to 5 accepts a whole class — 3 covers every 3xx, for an app that redirects to a login page. Anything else is a single code.
form.healthCheckExpectStatusError: Expected status must be 0, a class from 1 to 5, or a code in 100..599.
form.healthCheckHostHeaderHint: The Host the probe sends. Empty uses the route's own host, which is what real traffic carries. Set this when the backend expects a different name.
form.validationFailedGeneric: The form was not saved: a field is invalid.
form.healthCheckProbeHint: Runs one probe per upstream with the settings above. Nothing is saved.
form.healthCheckProbeNetworkError: The test could not be run.
form.healthCheckHeaderHostError: Set the Host in the field above, not as a header.
form.healthCheckHelper: Leave a field blank to use the server default (GET / 30s / 5s / passes=1 / fails=1). URI is required.
form.upstreamPrivateIPHint: Private IP + https detected — the upstream certificate is probably self-signed. Use "Advanced upstream TLS" if the connection fails.
form.tlsAdvancedHelper: Tick only if the upstream presents a self-signed certificate (homelab Proxmox, Synology DSM, ESXi, UniFi). In production, prefer adding the CA to Arenet host's trust store.
form.wafModeStart: Start with Detect to spot false positives before enforcing.
form.uploadStreamingHelper: Disables WAF inspection of the request body AND Caddy's in-RAM buffering. Enable for large uploads where the body would otherwise be staged in RAM (Docker registry, file servers, video transcoders). Request headers + URL + response stay scanned. Leave this toggle OFF for API/web routes where the body is small and should be scanned.
form.wafDisableCRSLabel: Disable OWASP CRS rules (trusted internal APIs)
form.wafDisableCRSHelper: Stops loading the OWASP Core Rule Set on this route. No more SQLi / XSS / RCE / LFI / Protocol rules. The WAF handler stays wired (dashboard counter + audit log intact) but Coraza no longer loads any rule, so none can trigger. Use only for trusted internal APIs (LAN) or legacy routes where the CRS generates recurring false-positives. The WAF mode (off/detect/block) is preserved and effective the moment the CRS is re-enabled.
form.wafExcludeRulesHelper: Disables only the listed CRS rules on this route; the rest of the Core Rule Set stays active. Use when a specific rule fires a false-positive on legitimate traffic. 6-digit IDs in [200000, 999999], excluding the [100000, 199999] Arenet-reserved range. Comma or space separators.
form.wafExcludeRulesIdentifyRules: To identify rules that fired on this route recently, see
form.wafExcludeRulesIdentifyRulesGeneric: To identify rules that fired recently, see
form.wafExcludeRulesCRSDisabledWarning: ⚠️ The CRS is disabled via the toggle above — exclusions are silent until re-enabled.
form.stateMaintenanceHint: Visitors get the maintenance page; the certificate stays alive and the bypass IPs still reach the backend.
form.stateRedirectHint: Answers a redirect; nothing is proxied.

redirect.targetHelper: Must be a different host. A target on this route's own name would redirect to itself — to send one path elsewhere on the same host, use a path rule instead.
redirect.code301Hint: Permanent. Browsers and search engines remember it.
redirect.code302Hint: Temporary. Nothing is cached; use it while you are unsure.
redirect.preservePathHelper: /a/b?c on this route lands on the same /a/b?c at the target. Off sends every visitor to the target as typed.
redirect.noProxyWarning: A redirecting route does not proxy: the WAF, authentication, rate limit and country block do not apply. TLS still does — the route needs its certificate to answer at all.

form.stateDisabledHint: The route is parked: its configuration is kept but nothing is served.
form.stateCreateHint: Maintenance becomes available once the route is saved.
form.wafExcludeTagsHelper: Disables every CRS rule carrying the listed tag on this route. More resilient than an ID list: a CRS update that adds rules to a tag automatically inherits the exclusion. Tag = a string with no spaces or commas inside (e.g. paranoia-level/3). Autocomplete suggests 24 common tags; any valid CRS tag is accepted.
form.rateLimitToggleLabelFull: Enable rate limiting (brute-force / API abuse protection)
form.rateLimitSentence: Beyond {events} requests per {window} from the same {key}, requests are refused with a 429.
form.rateLimitHelper: Beyond the maximum requests per period, requests are rejected with HTTP 429. Sliding-window algorithm (no hard reset at end of period). The default key {http.request.remote.host} resolves to the raw socket peer IP (no X-Forwarded-For trust — anti-spoof). On a deployment behind a trusted proxy, switch to {http.request.header.X-Forwarded-For} or similar.
form.errorPagesTemplateHelper: The Arenet branded default applies automatically to the 401 / 403 / 404 / 429 / 500 / 502 / 503 / 504 codes if no template is attached.
form.errorPagesOverrideNotice: {count} per-code override(s) are applied to this route and kept on save. Edit them in
form.errorPagesOverrideHelper: Overrides replace BOTH the template AND the default for the listed code. Leave blank to use the template or the default.
form.geoSentenceDeny: Blocked if the visitor comes from
form.geoSentenceAllow: Allowed only if the visitor comes from
form.geoSentenceEmpty: No rule yet: pick continents, countries or networks (ASN) below — one list is enough.
form.geoMatchTitleDeny: Block the visitor if they come from…
form.geoMatchTitleAllow: Allow the visitor only if they come from…
form.geoMatchHelper: Every list is optional and one match is enough: continent OR country OR network (ASN). Fill only what you need.
form.geoExceptionsHelper: These countries and networks pass even when a rule above matches them.
form.geoExceptionsHint: Countries let through even when their continent or the list blocks them — e.g. deny Asia except Japan.
form.geoASNNoDatabase: No ASN database installed yet: AS numbers are saved but won't match until the GeoLite2-ASN database is downloaded.
form.geoAllowEmptyError: Allow-list needs at least one country or continent — otherwise all public traffic would be blocked.
form.certSourceInternalHelper: Caddy issues a self-signed certificate from its internal CA. Browsers will show a trust warning unless the CA is imported.
form.certSourceManualNone: No uploaded certificate covers this host yet.
form.authNoneHint: Anyone who reaches the route is served.
form.authBasicHint: The browser asks for a username and password before anything reaches the backend.
form.authForwardHint: Every request is checked with your identity provider first (Caddy forward_auth).
form.authForwardDelegatesTo: The route's auth gate delegates to the identity provider at
form.wafModeDetect: Detect — log matches, let traffic through
form.wafModeOffHint: No inspection: requests go straight to the backend.
form.wafModeDetectHint: Requests are inspected and logged, never blocked. Start here to spot false positives.
form.wafModeBlockHint: Matching requests are refused with a 403 and logged.
form.countryBlockSearchPlaceholder: Type FR, DE, Russia, United States…
form.healthCheckLiveFailingHint: The probe is failing. Check the URI, the expected status and the expected body below — a probe that does not match what the backend answers takes the route out of service, even though the backend is up.
form.headersEmptyResponse: None — the response is returned as the backend sends it.
form.headersEmpty: None — the request is forwarded as it arrives.
form.disabledHelper: A disabled route keeps its config but serves no traffic (requests get the 404 page).

maintenance.retryAfterHelp: Sent as {seconds}s in the Retry-After header (browsers and bots read seconds).
maintenance.messagePlaceholder: e.g. Database migration in progress — back around 14:00.
maintenance.messageHelp: Shown on this route's maintenance page. Leave empty to use the global message (Settings → Error Pages → Maintenance).

confirm.title: Disable route?
confirm.text: This route will no longer serve traffic. Its configuration is preserved so you can re-enable it anytime.

lastHttps.title: Disable the last HTTPS route?
lastHttps.text: This is the last active HTTPS route. Disabling it stops the HTTPS server (port 443) — requests to any HTTPS URL will fail with connection refused. Continue?

ipFilter.offHint: No gate — traffic is not filtered by source IP.
ipFilter.cidrsHint: One IP or CIDR range per line, e.g. 192.168.1.10 or 10.0.0.0/8.

pathRules.sectionHelp: Apply extra protection — basic auth, a source-IP filter, a rate limit — to requests under a path prefix. These add to the route's own gates rather than replacing them.
pathRules.matchExactHelp: Off, the rule also covers everything under the path. On, it matches that one path and nothing else — which is what a rule on / needs, since the sub-tree form would also catch the redirect's own target.
pathRules.redirectTargetHelp: A path on this host (/admin/login) or a full URL elsewhere. It must fall OUTSIDE this rule's own path, or every visitor would be redirected to it forever — Arenet refuses that at save.
pathRules.redirectCodeHelp: 302 is temporary and is the right default for a landing path: nothing is cached, so an application update can change it. 301 is remembered by browsers and is hard to take back.
pathRules.basicAuthAdditiveHint: Applies in addition to the route's own authentication, which still runs first — it does not replace it.
pathRules.forwardAuthLabel: Require an identity provider for this path
pathRules.forwardAuthAdditiveHint: Applies in addition to the route's own authentication, which still runs first. Replaces this rule's username and password.
pathRules.forwardAuthNoProvider: No forward-auth provider is configured yet.
pathRules.authExemptLabel: Exempt this path from the route's authentication
pathRules.authExemptWarning: This path becomes reachable without signing in. That is the point of the control, and it is a deliberate opening.
pathRules.authExemptStillApplies: Everything else on the route still applies: WAF, CrowdSec, country filtering, IP filter and rate limit.
pathRules.authExemptHeaders: These identity headers are removed from incoming requests on this path, so a caller cannot forge one:
pathRules.rateLimitHint: Counted separately from the route's own limit, which still applies — a strict limit here does not throttle the rest of the route. Runs before this path's basic auth. Over the limit: 429.
pathRules.emptyRuleError: The rule on "{path}" carries nothing: add a rate limit, basic auth, an IP filter, an upstream or a redirect — or remove the rule.
pathRules.upstreamInheritHint: By default this path follows the route's upstream.

securityRoute.notFoundMiddle: does not exist (any more). Go back to the
securityRoute.wafOffTitle: The WAF is off for this route
securityRoute.wafOffMiddle: exists, but its WAF mode is off, so no security event is collected for it. Edit it from the
securityRoute.wafOffAfter: page and set the WAF to detect or block to start collecting.
securityRoute.disabledBody: The observability subsystem failed to start, so the WAF event history is missing. The proxy still blocks malicious requests according to the configured rules; only this dashboard is temporarily empty.
securityRoute.chartWafBlocksAria: WAF blocks per minute for this route
securityRoute.chart4xxAria: 4xx responses per minute for this route
securityRoute.chart5xxAria: 5xx responses per minute for this route
securityRoute.chartRequestsAria: Requests per minute for this route

securityRoute.rulesEmpty: No WAF event in the recent window for this route.

security.subtitle: Posture overview plus the CrowdSec drill-down (snapshot, live LAPI, scenarios).
security.tlsBanner: Granular TLS settings (minimum version, curves, ciphers, HTTP/3, OCSP, session tickets) are not exposed yet. Caddy's defaults are shown below.
security.headersEmptyTitle: A centralised security-header policy is not exposed by Arenet yet.
security.headersEmptyBodyBefore: Individual headers can be injected per route today, from the route form under
security.headersEmptyBodyAfter: . A global controller (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, CSP with nonce, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) is planned.

tcpServices.title: TCP / UDP services
tcpServices.subtitle: Relay raw TCP or UDP to a backend, with the real client IP preserved. Arenet never reads these bytes: the client and the backend negotiate end to end.
tcpServices.emptyBody: A layer-4 service forwards a port to a backend — a mail server, a database, SSH, WireGuard. Unlike a route, nothing is read on the way: no WAF, no error pages, and the encryption stays end to end.

form.name: Name
form.protocolTCPHint: Connections: mail, databases, SSH, RDP, most things.
form.protocolUDPHint: Datagrams: WireGuard, DNS, syslog, game servers. No active health check, and the PROXY header needs v2.
form.proxyNoneHint: The backend sees Arenet’s address, not the client’s.
form.proxyV1Hint: Text header. TCP only — v1 carries no UDP address.
form.proxyV2Hint: Binary header, TCP and UDP. The usual choice.
form.proxyCallout: The backend must be configured to expect this header from Arenet’s address, otherwise connections fail silently. On Stalwart that setting is proxyTrustedNetworks; on HAProxy, accept-proxy; on nginx, proxy_protocol on the listen line.
form.udpV1Refused: Refused: version 1 carries no UDP address. Use v2, or none.
form.crowdsecHelper: IPs banned on your HTTP routes are banned here too. Ignored when no bouncer is configured.
form.restrictHelper: Only the listed ranges reach the backend; everything else is closed. Leave off for a service the world must reach, such as inbound mail.
form.healthCheckHelper: A periodic connection; a backend that stops answering is taken out of the pool.
form.udpHealthCheckRefused: Refused over UDP: opening a UDP socket always succeeds, so the check could never fail.
form.disabledHelper: The service is kept but nothing is listening.
form.notApplicable: A relay forwards bytes without reading them: no WAF, no error pages, no country blocking. TLS stays negotiated end to end between the client and the backend.
form.udp_not_testable: UDP is connectionless: there is no handshake to attempt, so Arenet cannot prove this backend is reachable without speaking its protocol.
form.proxyNote: This service prepends the PROXY protocol {version} header. The backend must be configured to expect it from this host, or connections fail silently — on Stalwart that setting is proxyTrustedNetworks.
form.testProxyRefused: header refused — the backend is not expecting it
form.testProxyExplain: The test sends a real PROXY protocol header. A backend that is not configured for it hangs up; one that is stays open and waits for the client to speak.
form.acceptProtocolHint: Closes connections whose handshake is not this protocol, before they reach the backend. A correct backend already refuses garbage, so this is hardening — what it adds is that a scanner never gets through, and that repeated mismatches are counted. The list depends on the transport above.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this service?
deleteDialog.message: The port stops being served as soon as you confirm.

tcpServices.refusedTooltip: Connections closed by a guard before the backend. Not counted as connections: they never reached the relay.

map.emptyBody: Arcs are drawn as WAF, rate-limit, CrowdSec and authentication decisions happen. A quiet map means nothing has been blocked since this page was opened.
map.subtitle: Real-time geographic view of traffic sources and security decisions. WAF, throttle, CrowdSec and auth failures are drawn as coloured arcs from the source to this Arenet instance.
map.degradedBody1: The server position could not be detected automatically. Check that the GeoLite2-City database sits at
map.degradedBody3: ), then restart. You can also enter a position by hand in Settings → Server position.
map.lanPillTitle: Internal traffic (LAN/RFC1918) received since this page was opened. These events are not drawn on the world map: they originate from the Arenet instance itself.
map.countryPillTitle: Requests blocked by a per-route country rule since this page was opened. The counter matches the grey arcs on the map (same events).

dashboard.subtitle: Real-time traffic across your {count} routes, recent WAF events and upstream services. Window {window}.
dashboard.disabledBody: The observability subsystem failed to start. The proxy is still serving traffic; only the metric history is missing. Check the Arenet logs for the root cause.
dashboard.recentWafEmpty: No recent WAF events in the window.

users.subtitle: {total} account{plural_total} — {admins} admin{plural_admins}, {viewers} viewer{plural_viewers} · {oidc} OIDC, {local} local
users.emptyFilteredBody: No account matches the current search and filters. Widen them to see the others.
users.toastCopyFailed: Copy failed — select the text manually
users.roleConfirmPromoteBody: {username} will get full admin access (CRUD on routes, settings and users).
users.roleConfirmDemoteBody: {username} will lose write access. Demoting the last local admin is blocked (break-glass invariant).
users.deleteConfirmServiceBody: {username} and its API token will be revoked immediately. This action is irreversible.
users.deleteConfirmLocalBody: {username} will be permanently deleted and all its sessions invalidated. Deleting the last local admin is blocked (break-glass invariant).
users.rotateModalIntro: The old token will be revoked immediately. All clients will not be able to authenticate until updated with the new token.
users.rotateRevealedShownOnce: New token shown only once. Copy it now.

oidc.emptyBody: No identity provider configured. The /users table only shows local accounts until SSO is enabled in Settings.
oidc.testScopesMissing: IdP reached ({ms} ms) but missing scopes: {scopes}
oidc.testOk: IdP reached in {ms} ms — scopes OK

channels.emptyBody: Add a first channel (webhook or email) to start receiving notifications. Channels are then targeted by rules in the Rules tab.
channels.severityTooltipPrefix: Minimum severity filtered by this channel. {tooltip}
channels.confirmMessage: Delete channel "{name}"? This action is irreversible.

rules.emptyBody: Add a first rule (WAF blocks threshold, certificate expiry, or system health) to trigger automatic notifications every 30 seconds. At least one channel must exist first in the Channels tab.
rules.summaryTestSkipped: Rule "{name}": {sent} sent, {skipped} skipped (channel disabled or below min severity).
rules.lastEvalTooltipPendingEnabled: Not yet evaluated — the watcher polls every 30 seconds; wait for the next tick.
rules.lastEvalTooltipDisabled: Rule disabled — the watcher ignores it.
rules.lastFireTooltipNever: Never fired. The condition has not been met since creation, or the rule is still in cooldown. Use the Test button to force a send without waiting.
rules.confirmMessage: Delete rule "{name}"? This action is irreversible.

history.degradedNotice: Observability unavailable: alert history is not accessible. Check that metrics.db is open.
history.emptyFiltered: No event matches the current filters.
history.emptyNoFilters: No event recorded yet. Create a channel then a rule in the tabs above, then click Test to generate a first event.

channelModal.secretsLost: The webhook URL of this channel was lost by an earlier version of Arenet (an edit saved the masked value). Retype it to repair the channel.
channelModal.typeLockedAfterCreate: The type cannot be changed after creation.
channelModal.redactedHeadersNote: Header values are redacted by the API. Leave the displayed value "[redacted]" as-is to keep the existing secret.
channelModal.bodyTemplatePlaceholders: Leave empty to send the full event as JSON. Wrap any value in `json` so quotes and newlines cannot break the body — `{"text": {{ json .Subject }}}`, with no quotes of your own around it. Placeholders:
channelModal.helpHeloName: The name Arenet announces to the mail server. Leave empty to use this machine’s hostname, or the domain of the From address. A strict server refuses a name that is not fully qualified.
channelModal.errWebhookUrlScheme: URL must start with http:// or https://.
channelModal.errTimeoutRange: Timeout must be between 1 and 60 seconds.
channelModal.errSmtpPortRange: SMTP port must be between 1 and 65535.
channelModal.errFromEmail: The "From" address must be a valid email.
channelModal.errAtLeastOneTo: At least one "To" recipient is required.
channelModal.hintDiscordUrl: From your Discord channel: Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy Webhook URL. This URL is the credential — anyone holding it can post to the channel — so it is stored as a secret and shown redacted afterwards.
channelModal.errDiscordUrlRequired: A Discord webhook URL is required.
channelModal.hintDiscordMentions: Discord IDs, separated by commas or spaces — not names. Everyone listed is notified on every alert this channel sends.
channelModal.errDiscordMentionUser: "{value}" is not a user ID. Discord notifies only on numeric IDs: turn on Developer Mode, then right-click the member and choose Copy User ID.
channelModal.errDiscordMentionRole: "{value}" is not a role ID. Discord notifies only on numeric IDs: turn on Developer Mode, then right-click the role and choose Copy Role ID.
channelModal.errDiscordUrlHost: That does not look like a Discord webhook URL (it must start with https://discord.com/ or https://discordapp.com/).

ruleModal.certExpiryHelper: Combined with a threshold (e.g. operator < and value 14) in the evaluation form below, alerts when a certificate is expiring soon.
ruleModal.certRenewalHelper: Combined with a threshold > 0 in the evaluation form below, alerts on any ACME renewal failure (Let's Encrypt, ZeroSSL…) within the window. Default 24h — matches Let's Encrypt's retry cadence.
ruleModal.kindLockedAfterCreate: The type cannot be changed after creation.
ruleModal.channelsEmpty: No active channel available. Create one first in the Channels tab.
ruleModal.errNameSlug: Name must be lowercase, alphanumeric and dashes only (1-64 characters).
ruleModal.errCooldownRange: Cooldown must be between 30 seconds and 24 hours.
ruleModal.errThresholdNumeric: The threshold value must be numeric.
ruleModal.errExpectedEmpty: The expected value cannot be empty.
ruleModal.errWafWindowRange: The WAF window must be between 60 seconds and 24 hours.
ruleModal.errCertRenewalWindowRange: The renewal failure window must be between 60 seconds and 7 days.
ruleModal.labelManualCertDays: Warn this many days before expiry
ruleModal.hintManualCertDays: Counts your manually uploaded certificates expiring within that many days. The rule then compares that COUNT against your threshold — so “> 0” means “at least one”. ACME certificates are covered by the separate “certificate expiry” source, not this one.

audit.subtitle: Review authentication events and route mutations.
audit.emptyNoFiltersBody: Every configuration change — a route created, a certificate uploaded, a user added — is recorded here with its author and its before/after values.
audit.emptyFiltered: No audit events match the current filters.

setup.subtitle: Create the initial administrator account.
setup.infoBannerBody: Look in the Arenet server logs for a line starting with
setup.infoBannerBodySuffix: The token is regenerated on every restart while no administrator exists.
setup.errAdminExists: Setup unavailable: an administrator account already exists.

errorPages.subtitle: HTML templates served by Caddy for status codes 401/403/404/429/500/502/503/504. With no template attached to a route, the Arenet branded default applies automatically.
errorPages.emptyBody: All routes currently receive the Arenet branded default. Create a template to customise the error pages of one or several routes.
errorPages.btnDuplicateBuiltinTooltip: Create a new template based on the default
errorPages.btnDuplicateTooltip: Create a new template based on this one
errorPages.readOnlyBannerBody: — this template is the Arenet default. Click "Duplicate to customise" in the top right to create an editable copy.
errorPages.catchallToggleLabel: Use for hosts that are not configured in Arenet
errorPages.catchallHint: This template's 404 page will be served for a request reaching a host that matches no route at all. This does NOT affect your routes — for that, use the option above. Only one template can hold this at a time.
errorPages.varsHelp: These placeholders are substituted by Caddy at request time (not in the preview, which uses fake values).
errorPages.deleteModalBody: Deleting "{name}" is irreversible. Routes that reference it will revert to the Arenet branded default.
errorPages.toastReadOnly: The "Arenet default" template is read-only; use "Duplicate".

maintenance.subtitle: Global HTML page served on any route toggled into maintenance mode (HTTP 503).
maintenance.editorPlaceholder: Leave empty to serve the Arenet branded default…
maintenance.toastReset: Cleared — the branded default will be served until you Save
maintenance.errFailedLoad: failed to load the maintenance page
maintenance.errFailedSave: failed to save the maintenance page
maintenance.helpRetryAfter: {arenet.maintenance.retry_after_human} shows the per-route retry delay in words, substituted at serve time. It is empty when Retry-After is 0, so collapse the block around it with a :has(:empty) rule — the shipped example pages do.
maintenance.helpEmpty: An empty page means Arenet serves its branded default maintenance page.
maintenance.builtinTooltip: This is the built-in Arenet default page — editing it and clicking Save turns it into your custom page.
maintenance.messagePlaceholder: e.g. Database migration in progress — back around 14:00. Thanks for your patience.
maintenance.messageHelp: Default message shown on maintenance pages via the {arenet.maintenance.message} placeholder. A route that sets its own message (in its edit form) overrides this. Leave empty to show the generic default line.
maintenance.previewMessage: Preview: your global maintenance message appears here.

ph.retryAfterHuman: The same delay in words (“1 day”, “30 minutes”) — English only, and empty when Retry-After is 0
ph.message: The route's message, or this global message as fallback
ph.refreshMeta: Auto-refresh meta tag built from Retry-After (built-in default only; empty when Retry-After is 0)

errorPages.routeDefaultToggleLabel: Use for every route that has no template
errorPages.routeDefaultHint: Routes that keep “None (Arenet branded default)” will serve THIS template's pages instead of Arenet's built-in ones. A route that picks its own template still wins, and codes this template leaves blank fall back to Arenet's. Only one template can hold this at a time.

settingsSubcards.automationResetHelper: To disable the auto-classifier cleanly, use Reset (bottom left) — the BoltDB configuration is wiped and the LAPI writer is detached immediately (audit row automation_reset). The trigger rules below are not touched: you can keep your config for future re-activation.
settingsSubcards.automationResetDialogMessage: The auto-classifier will stop pushing decisions to LAPI immediately. The trigger rules are not touched — you can keep them for future re-activation. No impact on the CrowdSec bouncer configuration (read-side).
settingsSubcards.revokeSessionMessage: The other device will be signed out immediately.

oidcSettings.title: OIDC SSO
oidcSettings.subtitle: Delegate admin login to an external identity provider. Local login remains available regardless (break-glass).
oidcSettings.providerHelper: Choose your OIDC provider to display its logo on the sign-in button. Leave empty to use the generic logo. The choice does NOT influence the authentication logic — it is purely visual.
oidcSettings.issuerHelper: OIDC issuer URL (the issuer field of the discovery document). DO NOT include the /.well-known/openid-configuration suffix — Arenet appends it automatically (if you paste the full URL, the suffix is silently stripped server-side). Authentik: /application/o/<slug>/ ; Keycloak: /realms/<realm> ; Authelia: the deployment root.
oidcSettings.scopesHelper: Space- or comma-separated. openid is mandatory; email is required for the canonicalisation step.
oidcSettings.labelAcceptUnverifiedEmail: Accept unverified email on first login (advanced)
oidcSettings.acceptUnverifiedEmailHelper: Off by default. Enable only when your IdP does not assert email_verified=true on its ID tokens (Authentik admin-created accounts being the typical case) and you fully control IdP-side account creation. Relaxes the Δ7 guard for the allowlist Email-bootstrap pass — only safe when the IdP itself is trusted.
oidcSettings.allowlistSubtitle: Only emails on this list can log in via SSO. New entries are "pending" until the user's first login canonicalises them.
oidcSettings.allowlistAddHelper: To find the OIDC Subject ID, look it up in your IdP's admin console. Leaving this field empty uses email-bootstrap on first login (requires the IdP to emit email_verified=true).

crowdsecSettings.title: CrowdSec bouncer
crowdsecSettings.subtitle: IP-reputation gate. Reads block decisions from the LAPI and rejects connections from sources CrowdSec flagged. Bouncer runs in-process; no extra container needed if CrowdSec engine is already on this host.
crowdsecSettings.lapiUrlHelper: LAPI listen URL. http://127.0.0.1:8080 for an apt install on the same host; http://crowdsec:8080 for a sibling Docker container in the same compose network; or any custom URL the deployment exposes.
crowdsecSettings.apiKeyHelper: Generate with cscli bouncers add arenet on the CrowdSec host. The key is shown only once at creation; if lost, delete + re-add the bouncer.
crowdsecSettings.bouncerNameHelper: Cosmetic identifier. Must match the name used in cscli bouncers add.
crowdsecSettings.timeoutHelper: Per-request cap on LAPI calls. Range 1–60. Default 5.
crowdsecSettings.saveFooter: Save & apply hot-reloads the embedded Caddy without a process restart. Active routes drop the request only after the new bouncer creds are live, so there is no race window. To disable the bouncer cleanly, use Reset (bottom left) — the BoltDB configuration is wiped and the bouncer drops out of the data plane immediately (audit row crowdsec_reset).
crowdsecSettings.resetDialogMessage: The bouncer will stop gating traffic immediately. Routes remain protected by the WAF + rate-limiter, but the IP-reputation gate will be disabled. No impact on the Security Automation configuration (watcher credentials).
crowdsecSettings.restartRequiredTitle: Restart Arenet for the new LAPI address to take effect
crowdsecSettings.restartRequiredBody: The address is saved, but the bouncer keeps using the previous one until the process restarts — it reports the new address in the log while still contacting the old one. Until you restart, CrowdSec blocks nothing: the bouncer fails open by design, so traffic keeps flowing unprotected and nothing else here will tell you.

geoipSettings.title: GeoIP database
geoipSettings.subtitle: Download and auto-update the MaxMind GeoIP database used by geoblocking and the world map.
geoipSettings.licenseKeyHelper: Your MaxMind license key. Leave blank to keep the stored one.
geoipSettings.resetDialogMessage: This clears the stored account ID and license key. Auto-update will stop until you configure them again.
geoipSettings.enablePaused: Auto-update is paused — MaxMind credentials are no longer configured. Restore them to resume.

backupSection.title: Backup & restore
backupSection.subtitle: Export the entire Arenet configuration as JSON, or restore from a previously-exported file.
backupSection.exportHelper: Default export redacts secrets (admin password hashes, OVH keys, OIDC client secret, forward-auth client secrets, per-route Basic Auth hashes). Use "Include secrets" only for disaster-recovery archives that you can store securely.
backupSection.restoreHelper: Choose a previously-exported file. The restore is all-or-nothing: any validation failure aborts before any change is written to storage.
backupSection.allowIncompleteHelper: Sentinels that cannot inherit from this instance will be cleared. Affected secrets need to be re-saved.
backupSection.allowEmptyUsersHelper: Accept a backup with zero users; the next boot will re-trigger the setup-token flow.
backupSection.confirmDialogMessage: Every secret in the file (password hashes, DNS credentials, TLS private keys, OIDC / forward-auth / CrowdSec secrets, alert channel credentials, service-account token hashes) is encrypted with this passphrase. Keep it safe: without it the file can only be restored without its secrets.
backupSection.restorePassphraseHelper: This backup is encrypted: enter the passphrase chosen at export.

scheduledBackups.title: Scheduled backups
scheduledBackups.subtitle: Arenet backs up its configuration on its own: to a folder (local disk or a mounted NAS share) and / or by email. Every file is encrypted with the passphrase below.
scheduledBackups.timeZoneHint: Server time zone: {tz}. In Docker it is UTC unless TZ is set (e.g. TZ=Europe/Paris).
scheduledBackups.dirHelper: Absolute path. To keep backups off this machine, mount a NAS share (NFS / SMB, or a Docker volume) and enter its path. Arenet checks it can write there when you save.
scheduledBackups.passphraseChangeLabel: New passphrase (leave empty to keep the current one)
scheduledBackups.passphraseHelper: Keep this passphrase in your password manager: it is the only way to restore these files on another machine.
scheduledBackups.noEmailChannel: No email alert channel yet: create one in Settings > Alerting first.
scheduledBackups.alertChannelsHelper: A failed backup always shows in the notification bell; it is also sent to the channels checked here.
scheduledBackups.confirmRestoreMessage: The current configuration will be replaced by {file}. Arenet reloads right away and rolls back on failure.
scheduledBackups.confirmDeleteMessage: {file} will be deleted from the backup folder.
scheduledBackups.errPassphraseRequired: Set a passphrase to enable scheduled backups.
scheduledBackups.errOldPassphrase: This file was encrypted with a previous passphrase: download it and restore it from Backup & restore with that passphrase.

routeCheck.title: Route check after save
routeCheck.subtitle: After every save, Arenet sends one real request to the route through its own proxy.
routeCheck.enabledHelper: A change that makes a working route stop answering (502 / 503 / 504) is undone automatically; a route that did not answer before either is kept, with a warning. New and re-enabled routes are never undone. A save may take up to ~10 s when the route does not answer.

serverPosition.title: Server position
serverPosition.subtitle: Center of the threat map (page /map). Detected automatically at startup via ipify + GeoLite2, or set manually below.
serverPosition.degradedBody: Automatic detection did not find the GeoLite2-City database. Place it at /var/lib/arenet/GeoLite2-City.mmdb (or set the ARENET_GEOIP_MMDB env var), then click "Re-detect" — or enter a manual position below.
serverPosition.toastDetectFailed: Detection failed: MMDB missing or ipify offline. Degraded state.

crowdsecDecisions.panelSubtitle: Arenet-side snapshot of the decisions received from LAPI.
crowdsecDecisions.mirrorNotConfiguredBody: The CrowdSec bouncer on the Caddy side and the StreamBouncer consumer on the Arenet side share the same LAPI key.
crowdsecDecisions.emptyActive: No active decision. The bouncer is not blocking any source currently.
crowdsecDecisions.emptyWindow: No decision in the window. The bouncer has never received a decision from LAPI.
crowdsecDecisions.liveNotConfiguredBody: The bouncer is not configured. Go to
crowdsecDecisions.liveNotConfiguredSuffix: to enter the LAPI URL and the bouncer key.
crowdsecDecisions.liveStaleNotice: Showing data from: last successful polling (the table
crowdsecDecisions.liveStaleNoticeSuffix: may be slightly out of date)
crowdsecDecisions.emptyLiveAll: No active decision according to LAPI. The bouncer is watching but no source is currently blocked. (CAPI sync runs every ~2-15 min; a freshly-started bouncer may take a few minutes to receive the community blocklist.)
crowdsecDecisions.emptyLiveFiltered: No decision in this category ({total} total — see the {tabAll} tab).
crowdsecDecisions.scenariosSubtitle: CrowdSec scenarios that fired over the last
crowdsecDecisions.automationNotConfiguredFooter: independently — this coupling only concerns the tab
crowdsecDecisions.scenariosEmptyHelp: Either no attack detected, or Arenet logs not yet

createServiceAccount.revealedSuffix: . Copy it now — it will never be retrievable again. Rotation generates a new token.
createServiceAccount.toastCopyFailed: Copy failed — select the text manually

apiDocs.confirmMutating: This request changes the real configuration of this Arenet (same effect as from the UI). Send it?

wafSecLang.title: SecLang (advanced)
wafSecLang.hint: Write your own Coraza rules for this route. For safety only SecRule, SecAction and SecMarker are accepted, with rule IDs 130000–139999, and nothing that reads files, runs programs or turns the WAF off. Rules run before the OWASP CRS and follow the route's WAF mode. Saved with the route.
wafSecLang.saveRefused: The SecLang was refused — see the problems under the editor.

tester.title: Test a request
tester.saveFirst: Save the route first to test requests against it.
tester.accepted: Accepted — no rule blocks this request

mode.detect: The route is in Detect mode: the request would only be logged.
mode.off: The WAF is off on this route: nothing would happen.

importCaddyfile.title: Import a Caddyfile
importCaddyfile.hint: Paste your Caddyfile (or drop the file). Arenet reads it with Caddy's own parser, shows what it would create, and writes nothing until you confirm.
importCaddyfile.replace: replace the existing route (its WAF, geo and rate-limit settings are lost)

wafRules.title: Custom rules
wafRules.hint: Block requests that match your own criteria (path, method, User-Agent, header). A rule follows the route's WAF mode: blocked (403) in Block mode, only logged in Detect mode. Saved with the route.
wafRules.wafOff: The WAF is off on this route: rules are kept but do nothing until you choose Detect or Block.
wafRules.conditionsLabel: Block when ALL these conditions match
wafRules.valuesLabel: Values (one per line — any of them)

user_agent.missing: the User-Agent is absent or empty

errors.name: Give the rule a name (up to 64 characters, no quotes or backslash).
errors.headerName: Header name: letters, digits, - or _ only.
errors.tooManyValues: Too many values for one condition.
errors.value: Values can't contain a double quote, a backslash or line breaks, and are at most 256 characters.
errors.path: A path must start with / (use “contains” otherwise).

wafExclude.title: Exclude rule {rule}
wafExclude.intro: Rule {rule} will stop inspecting the {kind} “{name}”. It keeps protecting every other field of the route.
wafExclude.pathInvalid: The path must start with / and contain no space, quote or backslash.
wafExclude.noEventPath: The event's path can't be used as-is: the exclusion will apply on every path of the route.
wafExclude.wholeRouteTitle: The field that triggered the rule is unknown
wafExclude.wholeRouteBody: This event doesn't say which field triggered the rule (older event, or a rule on the URL itself). The exclusion will disable rule {rule} on the whole route {host}.
wafExclude.detectHint: Tip: check a few more events before excluding — a real attack can look like a false positive.
wafExclude.toastExists: This exclusion already exists on the route.

editor.title: Targeted exclusions
editor.hint: A targeted exclusion keeps the rule active but stops it from inspecting one field — the recommended way to fix a false positive. Create them from a WAF event (Logs or route Security page, “Exclude…”) or add one here.
editor.removeAria: Remove the exclusion of rule {rule} for {name}
editor.errRule: Enter a CRS rule ID (200000–999999). Initialization and blocking-evaluation rules (901, 949, 959, 980) can't be excluded.
editor.errName: Field name required, without space, comma, semicolon, quote, backslash or pipe, and not starting with /.
editor.errPath: The path must start with / and contain no space, quote or backslash.
editor.errDuplicate: This exclusion is already in the list.

banIp.title: Ban an IP
banIp.maskWarn: ⚠ You are about to ban {count} IPs.
banIp.reasonPlaceholder: Why this ban? (visible in the audit log)
banIp.notConfiguredBody: Manual ban uses the watcher credentials from Security Automation. Go to
banIp.notConfiguredSuffix: and enter your watcher ({cmd} on the CrowdSec host).

certs.pageSubtitle: ACME-managed TLS certificates. Wildcard apex configuration ships under managed domains; per-route certs are auto-provisioned by certmagic when TLS is enabled.
certs.renewalHelper: All certificates are automatically renewed by certmagic (Caddy v2) ~30 days before expiry, with exponential retry on failure. No manual action required. Renewal logs are available on the {logsLink} page.
certs.certsLoadError: Could not fetch certificates (backend returned an error). The rest of this page remains usable.
certs.certsEmptyHelper: Certificates are auto-provisioned when a TLS route is created or when a managed apex is declared.
certs.staleBadgeTooltip: Last failure: {ago} · {count} attempt{plural} without successful renewal. Click to view history.
certs.policiesLead: A managed apex issues ONE wildcard certificate via DNS-01 (covers every subdomain route). The DNS provider is configured under {settingsLink}.
certs.dnsUnconfiguredHelper: Wildcard issuance is disabled — covered routes will serve self-signed certs from Caddy's internal CA until you configure the DNS provider in
certs.policiesIssuingHint: The certificate is being requested (DNS-01). This page refreshes on its own.
certs.policiesFoot: Declaring an apex marks every existing route under *.<apex> as covered by the wildcard. The per-route ACME selector is hidden in the route editor, and the certificate is provisioned once for every subdomain.
certs.mdDeleteLead: Covered routes' ACMEChallenge will be reverted. Pick the post-revert challenge value below.
certs.mdDeleteWarning: Heads up. Each covered route will request its own HTTP-01 cert on the next reload. Many routes on one apex may hit Let's Encrypt's per-domain rate limit (50 certs / week).
certs.drillEmpty: No lifecycle event observed for this domain in the retention window (90 days).
certs.drillLead: The {count} most recent event{plural} for this domain, newest first.
certs.wizardApexHint: Bare domain (no leading *.) — the wildcard is implied. Issues a cert for {wildcard}.
certs.wizardIncludeApexLabel: Include bare apex in cert SAN

emptyState.ctaLabel: Configure a DNS provider in Settings

confirm.title: Delete certificate
confirm.text: Permanently delete the certificate for {domain}? The .crt/.key/.json files will be removed from disk. This is irreversible.

blocked.title: Cannot delete
blocked.text: The certificate for {domain} is in use by: {routes}. Delete or disable those route(s) first.

generate.title: Generate a CSR
generate.sansHelp: Comma-separated list of additional DNS names (e.g. www.example.com, api.example.com).
generate.keyAlgorithmRSAHelp: Compatible with all CAs including legacy PKI (Windows AD CS).
generate.keyAlgorithmECDSAHelp: Faster handshakes, smaller key. Some legacy CAs reject ECDSA — verify support first.

pending.empty: No CSR is waiting for a signed certificate.
pending.multiplePendingHint: Each pending row was generated by a "Generate CSR" request. Download the CSR, submit it to your CA, then upload the signed certificate here.
pending.deleteConfirmText: This permanently deletes the generated private key. If your CA signs the certificate later you will NOT be able to import it — you'll need to generate a new CSR.

external.title: External certificates
external.lead: Upload certificates issued by an external CA (e.g. DigiCert, enterprise PKI). Arenet stores them and makes them available to routes as a manual certificate source.
external.loadError: Could not fetch external certificates (backend returned an error). The rest of this page remains usable.

upload.certHelp: Your domain's certificate — the "leaf" (e.g. your_domain.crt / cert.pem / fullchain.pem). If your CA gave you a single "fullchain" file with several certificates, paste it all here and leave Chain empty — Arenet splits the leaf from the intermediates automatically.
upload.chainHelp: The CA's intermediate certificate(s) that link your certificate to a trusted root (e.g. intermediate.crt / ca-bundle.crt / chain.pem). Leave empty if you pasted a fullchain above, or if your CA didn't provide intermediates.
upload.keyHelp: The private key generated with your CSR (e.g. your_domain.key / privkey.pem). It never leaves Arenet and is never shown again after upload.
upload.requiredError: Name, certificate and private key are required.

errors.chainSpecifiedTwice: The chain is specified twice. You pasted a full chain in the Certificate field AND filled the Chain field. Put the intermediates in only ONE place — clear the Chain field, or paste only the leaf certificate above.
errors.keyDoesNotMatchCert: The private key does not match the certificate. Check you pasted the key that was generated with this certificate's CSR.
errors.invalidCertPem: The Certificate field is not a valid PEM certificate.
errors.invalidChainPem: The Chain field is not a valid PEM certificate.
errors.keyRequired: The Private key (PEM) field is required.

confirm.title: Delete external certificate
confirm.text: Permanently delete the certificate "{name}"? This is irreversible.
confirm.revokeNotice: Removing this certificate from Arenet does NOT revoke it with the issuing CA. If the private key may be compromised, contact your certificate authority directly to request revocation.

blocked.title: Cannot delete
blocked.text: The certificate "{name}" is in use by: {routes}. Delete or disable those route(s) first.

waf.pageSubtitle: The Coraza engine applies the OWASP Core Rule Set. Event counts shown below reflect blocked requests over the last 24h, per category.
waf.disabledHelper: WAF event counts are surfaced via the observability subsystem, which failed to start. Coraza is still inspecting traffic; only the dashboard projection is missing.
waf.categoriesReadOnlyNotice: Granular category control (enable/disable per category) is deferred to a future step. Counts shown below are read-only.
waf.drillEmpty: No rule triggered in this category in the last 24h.
waf.ipEnforcementHelper: The full timeline of blocked IPs (auto + manual). Manual list management is deferred (see backlog).

topology.emptyBody: The graph shows your hostnames, the Arenet hub and the backends behind it, with live traffic on the links. Create a route and it appears here within seconds.
topology.title: Topology
topology.lede: Reverse-proxy entry points on the left, upstream services on the right. The thickness and brightness of each line reflect the real-time throughput of that flow.

sidebar.legendWarn: high latency (p99 > 300 ms) or a few 5xx
sidebar.legendNote: Thickness is computed on the 60-second rolling average. The animation points in the dominant traffic direction — incoming requests towards the services.

logs.pageSubtitle: Real-time stream of WAF events, throttling, authentication failures and certificate lifecycle. Full 2xx/3xx traffic capture is deferred — see backlog.
logs.emptyNoEventsBody: Requests, WAF decisions, rate-limit hits and authentication failures land here as they happen. Widen the window, or send some traffic through a route.
logs.emptyNoEvents: No events in the current window.

system.title: Host
system.sourceContainer: the container's limit, not the machine's memory

createUser.roleHelp: A viewer can look at everything and change nothing. Grant admin deliberately.
createUser.generate: Let Arenet generate the first password
createUser.mustChangeNotice: Whoever creates the account knows its first password, so the account is required to change it at first login.
createUser.revealIntro: Copy this now. It is shown once and nothing can retrieve it afterwards — if you lose it, delete the account and create it again.
createUser.revealWarning: The account must change this password the first time it signs in.
createUser.toastCopyFailed: Could not copy — select the text and copy it by hand

mustChange.title: Change your password
mustChange.body: This account was created by an administrator, who knows its first password. Choose your own before going any further.

observability.latencyAria: Server time and total time, in milliseconds
observability.latencyHint: The gap between the two lines is the response transfer: the server had finished, the visitor was still downloading. A gap in a line means that bucket held too few requests for the chosen quantile.
observability.quantileAria: Which quantile the latency lines report
